cmgdr

A small, low-level R client for the public curatedMetagenomicData (cMD) data releases at https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org. It is for the cMD team and anyone who wants the published profiles quickly: find a release, list its tables and studies, download verified files, read per-study files, build a species TreeSummarizedExperiment, or attach the whole release in DuckDB and query it with SQL or dplyr.

It only knows the published layout (JSON indexes, Parquet, TSV and a read-only DuckLake catalog). Higher-level tooling can build on it.

Install

cmgdr is being prepared for Bioconductor. Until it is accepted, install it from GitHub:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("seandavi/cmgdr")

Once it is on Bioconductor:

BiocManager::install("cmgdr")

Imports are only curl, digest and jsonlite. Optional:

  • duckdb and DBI for cmgd_connect() and reading Parquet files (install.packages("duckdb"), duckdb 1.5.4.1 or newer);
  • TreeSummarizedExperiment and Matrix for cmgd_species_tse() (BiocManager::install("TreeSummarizedExperiment"));
  • dplyr and dbplyr to query attached tables with dplyr.

Quick start 

library(cmgdr)

cmgd_datasets()                      # published datasets and their latest release
rel <- cmgd_release("cmgd_nextflow-2.2.1")   # latest release
rel

cmgd_tables(rel)                     # tables, row counts, licence
cmgd_studies(rel)                    # studies and sample counts

# Per-study files: downloaded once into a checksum-verified cache
qc <- cmgd_read_study(rel, "ZellerG_2014", "qc")
tse <- cmgd_species_tse(rel, "ZellerG_2014")   # species x samples, sparse

# The whole release in DuckDB, nothing downloaded up front
con <- cmgd_connect(rel)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT study_name, count(*) AS n FROM qc_metrics GROUP BY 1")
dplyr::tbl(con, "taxonomic_profile_metaphlan")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

# HUMAnN gene families (HUMAnN datasets only), one file per sample
gf_rel <- cmgd_release("cmgd_humann3.9-2.3.0")
cmgd_genefamilies(gf_rel)            # studies with gene families
gf <- cmgd_genefamilies(gf_rel, study = "ZellerG_2014")   # fetches only that study's index
cmgd_download(gf_rel, gf$url[1])

See vignette("cmgdr") for a walk through, and the publisher’s consumer guide (docs/data-access.md in seandavi/nextflow_telemetry) for what every table and column holds.

What it reads 

https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org/index.json   every dataset, latest release
https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org/<dataset>/
  latest.json, releases.json
  <release>/manifest.json, catalog.ducklake
  <release>/tables/<table>/files.json, schema.json, data/*.parquet
  <release>/studies/index.json, studies/<study>/...
  <release>/genefamilies/index.json, <study>.json   -> files on https://cmgd-raw.cancerdatasci.org

A dataset is one pipeline registration, named <workflow_id>-<version> (cmgd_nextflow-2.2.1, cmgd_humann3.9-2.3.0, …). A release is an immutable snapshot named by its build date (2026-10-08). Neither site can be listed; everything is found through the JSON indexes. cmgdr refuses a manifest whose publication spec major version (cdsci-lake, 2) or a cmgd index whose spec_version major (cmgd index spec, 1) it does not know.

Downloads go to tools::R_user_dir("cmgdr", "cache") (see cmgd_cache_dir()), are checked against the indexes’ size and SHA-256 and are not fetched again while the cached copy verifies. The per-study gene-family indexes are verified against genefamilies/index.json, which is verified against studies/index.json.

Development

Install the package’s dependencies, including the Suggests the tests and vignette need (webfakes, duckdb, TreeSummarizedExperiment, …), then run the tests. No credentials or network are needed: the tests serve a local fixture site.

pak::local_install_dev_deps()
testthat::test_local()   # or R CMD check

Code follows the tidyverse style with 4-space indents and lines of at most 80 characters (Bioconductor’s style). A pre-commit hook runs styler on staged R files; enable it once per clone with

pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install

Conformance

The tests run against a small fixture release, shipped as one archive (tests/testthat/fixtures/site.tar.gz), generated by the publisher’s own code (data-raw/make_fixture.sh, which records the nextflow_telemetry commit it came from), unpacked under tempdir() and served over local HTTP with Range support. The fixture is the contract: when the release layout changes, regenerate it and fix whatever breaks.
